title: Entropy-Guided Resetting for Generation Optimization
one_line_claim: Shannon entropy of token distributions signals conversational context drift; entropy-guided resetting of context restores performance across multi-turn tasks.
method_summary: ERGO monitors the Shannon entropy H = -∑P(v)logP(v) of per-token probability distributions during generation, computing delta entropy ΔH(t) = H(t) - H(t-1) at configurable turn granularity. When ΔH exceeds a learned threshold τ (calibrated per model/task), the system rewrites or consolidates the conversation context before resuming generation. Results span 5 LLMs and 5 task types (code, database, math, data-to-text, actions).

key_findings.quote: Fig. 1 demonstrates the cumulative benefits of entropy-guided context management. Across all models and tasks, we observe an average 56.6% improvement in task performance compared to the FULL single-turn baseline and 18.3% improvement over the SHARED multi-turn baseline.
key_findings.finding: ERGO achieves 56.6% average performance improvement across five multi-turn tasks relative to the full-context baseline.

key_findings.quote: On the aptitude metrics, ERGO achieves a 24.7% increase in peak performance capability (90th percentile) and a 35.3% reduction in performance variability (unreliability score) compared to the FULL baseline.
key_findings.finding: ERGO reduces performance variability by 35.3% (unreliability metric) compared to single-turn baseline, and achieves 24.7% improvement in peak performance (90th percentile aptitude).

key_findings.quote: Ablation studies (Section 5.3) confirm that entropy-guided triggering (τ=0.03) significantly outperforms: (1) random resetting at equivalent frequency, (2) fixed-interval resets regardless of entropy, and (3) no resetting. Correlation analysis in Table 3 shows strong negative correlation between ΔH and performance maintenance (r = -0.81 for Llama 3.1 70B on Database task), validating entropy as a degradation signal.
key_findings.finding: Entropy-guided threshold resetting outperforms both random resetting and fixed-interval baselines; entropy signal correlates strongly with performance degradation (r=0.81 Llama 3.1 70B on Database task).

relation_to_herald.shared: Both use zero-cost runtime signals (entropy for ERGO, logit distributions for HERALD) to detect model degradation without external oracles or ground truth. Both operate during inference on per-token or per-turn granularity, enabling lightweight monitoring of generation quality. Both target categorical failure modes (conversational drift vs. KV-cache compression artifacts) as detectable discontinuities in signal behavior.
differs_on: Failure mode: ERGO detects conversational context drift and instruction amnesia in multi-turn settings; HERALD detects compression-induced catastrophes (looping, non-termination) in single-pass constrained-KV generation.
Intervention target: ERGO resets or rewrites user-facing context (prompt consolidation); HERALD intervenes at the compression scheduler to adjust KV-eviction thresholds upstream.

Detection mechanism: ERGO uses a scalar entropy threshold τ calibrated per model/task; HERALD uses a time-series XGBoost classifier trained on multivariate logit features (variance, skewness, entropy, concentration metrics) with prediction horizon.
